newsitem.title: UK: Argentina cancelled jumbo bond "salutary lesson".
newsitem.headline: Argentina cancelled jumbo bond "salutary lesson".

text.p: Argentina's decision to cancel a jumbo dollar bond may prove a valuable lesson to underwriters not to be overly aggressive when bidding for mandates, bankers said on Tuesday.
"It's a salutary lesson to bankers that regular and sophisticated borrowers like Argentina will not necessarily allow underwriters to backtrack on commitments," a syndicate manager said.
"If they said they could do a bond at a certain spread and then don't deliver the borrower will go elsewhere and it's a good message," he added.
In recent months, the investor quest for yield and emerging market borrowers' significant need for funds coupled with investment banks' desire for business have seen launch spreads squeezed tighter.

Overnight in Argentina, the Economy Ministry's director of credit, Federico Molina, said the country cancelled plans to issue a new global bond due 2004 because it did not want to pay the premium demanded by investors after currency volatility in South East Asia.
"Investors are asking for a premium because of the volatility after Thailand. Therefore we decided to cancel because we did not want to pay this premium," Molina said.
CSFB and SBC Warburg were awarded the mandate for the transaction on July 14. Two days later it was announced the country would delay the global bond because of market volatility.

Unofficial price talk at the time the planned bond was announced was 185 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, but spread speculation widened to around 200 b.p. over because of the market volatility.
"It was over-aggressive bidding for a transaction. The only way deals are getting done at the moment is with concessionary pricing," an emerging markets syndicate official said.
Another dealer said: "They were mandated and won the bid at a spread they could not deliver, so the borrower went somewhere else...it tells its own story."
So instead, Argentina decided to increase a $1.0 billion 8.375 percent December 2003 global bond by $500 million to yield 185 basis points over similar dated U.S. Treasuries via Salomon Brothers.
The bond was originally launched in 1993.
The deal was done at a 25 basis point concession, as it traded as tightly as 160 b.p. last night, dealers said.
Bankers welcomed Argentina's change of strategy and said it was better to increase the liquidity of an existing benchmark than foist an unwanted seven-year on the market at the wrong price.

"The two underwriters were mandated a spread that would not, nor could not, have made any sense in the current market environment so actually this was quite an elegant solution," a syndicate official said.
"There was already an existing trading level for the 2003's and the increase was priced at a sensible concession to that," he added.
"It removed the possibility of an over-aggressive new seven-year deal being foisted on the market."
